answers.answer: A Swift library for declaring command-line interfaces using property wrappers and command types: it parses arguments, instantiates commands, invokes run(), and supplies help/errors. Application developers import ArgumentParser; users run the resulting executables. Repository examples include repeat, roll and math; the README also identifies swift-format and Swift Package Manager as adopters (not independently inspected here).

ArgumentParser supplies the command API and parsing/execution machinery. CommandParser builds/traverses command types, uses LenientParser and ArgumentDecoder, and validates decoded commands. SplitArguments tokenizes the vector. ArgumentParserToolInfo holds versioned Codable command/argument descriptions. ArgumentParserTestHelpers supplies test assertions and expectation-backed commands. The GenerateManual and GenerateDoccReference plugins invoke corresponding generator executables; generate-manual reads a tool's dumped help and renders manual pages. Examples and test targets exercise the library.

Implementation/examples are Swift. SwiftPM's Package.swift declares tools-version 6.0, no external package dependencies, the ArgumentParser library product and two plugin products; internal library, executable and test targets form the module boundaries. An alternative CMake build requires 3.19 and enables C and Swift; its comment says C is enabled for a GNUInstallDirs workaround, not evidence of a C implementation. CMake includes Sources, optional Examples and Tests.

Examples/repeat/Repeat.swift declares @main struct Repeat: ParsableCommand. Swift's generated entry invokes the inherited static main(); its source implementation calls self.main(nil). Repeat's application behavior begins in mutating run(). The generated executable entry itself is not checked-in source.

Sources/ArgumentParser/Parsable Types/ParsableCommand.swift, extension ParsableCommand, static main(_ arguments: [String]?): try parseAsRoot(arguments), then try command.run(), catching errors with exit(withError:). parseAsRoot creates CommandParser(self) and calls parse(arguments:). main() forwards nil. DEBUG builds additionally reject invalid async-command hierarchies.

generate-manual directly depends on ArgumentParser and ArgumentParserToolInfo. Package.swift lists both in that executable target's dependencies; GenerateManual.swift imports both, conforms to ParsableCommand, and decodes ToolInfoHeader/ToolInfoV0. Thus edges run from generate-manual to the two libraries. The separate GenerateManual plugin depends on generate-manual, not conversely. Foundation is also imported but is not an internal package target.

Source-derived successful path: Repeat @main -> inherited main() -> main(nil) -> parseAsRoot -> CommandParser.parse -> parseBesidesCustomCompletion -> SplitArguments -> descendingParse -> parseCurrent (LenientParser, ArgumentDecoder, command-type init(from:)) -> validate -> extractLastParsedValue -> existential command.run(). The input becomes ["hello"]; phrase is hello, absent count stays nil and includeCounter false. Repeat.run uses count ?? 2 and prints hello twice. Repeat inherits an empty/default-subcommand-free configuration. Dispatch limits: @main entry and Decodable synthesis are compiler-generated; init(from:), validate and run use command/protocol dispatch. This traces source-supported intended behavior, not a captured runtime stack or exhaustive possible dispatch targets.

Direct SwiftPM consumers of ArgumentParserToolInfo are ArgumentParser, ArgumentParserTestHelpers, generate-docc-reference, generate-manual, and ArgumentParserToolInfoTests. Each explicitly names it in dependencies. The other examples/tests/plugins may be transitively affected, but are not direct consumers according to this manifest.

The Repeat example exercises X: its @main ParsableCommand enters inherited main(), which parses then calls run(); Repeat implements the synchronous printing behavior. This is a source-backed example, not a test execution claim. A guessed RepeatTests.swift URL failed, so no specific test from that path is asserted.

For process input, Platform.swift snapshots CommandLine.arguments into CommandLine._staticArguments. parseAsRoot uses Array(_staticArguments.dropFirst()) when no explicit vector is supplied; explicitly supplied [String] bypasses that removal. CommandParser.parse first handles custom-completion input, then parseBesidesCustomCompletion constructs SplitArguments. Its initializer preserves originalInput, tokenizes each string with parseIndividualArg, tracks origins, classifies values/options/--, expands possible short-option packs, and treats everything after -- as values. descendingParse then decodes commands. OS/Swift-runtime construction of CommandLine.arguments is outside these inspected repository sources.
